subtopic: Prefill vs decode / Compute vs memory characterization
learningObjective: Distinguish the compute and memory characteristics of prefill and decode phases in autoregressive LLM inference.
stem: Which characterization of prefill vs decode in a batch-1 LLM inference is correct?

options.text: Both prefill and decode are memory-bandwidth bound because both phases read the same model weights from HBM per forward pass; the difference in wall time between them reflects only the number of tokens processed.
Prefill is memory-bound (streaming weights once) and decode is compute-bound (each token performs a full transformer forward with high arithmetic intensity on cached KV).

Prefill (processing a prompt of P tokens together) is typically compute-bound on the QKV / MLP GEMMs because arithmetic intensity per weight scales with P; decode (batch-1, one token at a time) is memory-bandwidth bound because each linear layer becomes a batch-1 GEMV with intensity ~1 flop/byte.

Prefill and decode both incur the same arithmetic intensity because they use the same weights and the same operators; the choice of prefill vs decode is entirely a scheduling artifact with no impact on where the bottleneck lies.

explanation: Prefill: a prompt of P tokens is processed simultaneously. Each weight matrix W is used with a [P, D] input, so intensity per weight fetch scales with P; for even modest P this pushes prefill into the compute-bound region (GEMM). Decode: one new token per step at batch-1 means each weight matrix is used against a single [1, D] activation — a GEMV with ~1 flop/byte, well below the ridge point. This is the classic asymmetry that drives all decode-oriented optimizations (batching, quantization, speculative decoding).

optionExplanations.C: Correct: prefill compute-bound, decode memory-bandwidth bound.
optionExplanations.A: Wrong: intensity differs by a factor of P between the two phases.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: reverses the direction — decode is memory-bound, not compute-bound.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: arithmetic intensity depends on the activation shape at that step.

assumptions: Batch size 1 for a single request; batching changes decode intensity.
nonImplications: Does not imply prefill is always faster than decode per token; prefill still processes many tokens.
Does not imply decode is always memory-bound at large batch; with big batch it can become compute-bound.
